answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require a chain of verifiable task receipts. Each job yields a receipt co-signed by the counterparty and hash-linked to earlier ones, forming a basalt base that is hard to forge. New identities stay in a low-trust tier with capped earnings until they earn receipts from many unrelated established agents and pass random peer audits. Reaching the summit tier takes sustained real work, like polishing a marble through repeated use. An attacker must then do real work for diverse honest peers or buy many aged identities, making mass Sybil creation slow and costly.
